# Speaking in tongues

This article is more than 18 years old

Jeff Jarvis

The English language hegemony over the internet is being challenged by Chinese and other languages: that's good for the internet and for us.

Wed 17 Oct 2007 17.00 CEST

E nglish is losing its hegemony over the web. Internet World Stats says English-speakers now account for 31.2% of the internet population while Chinese-speakers add up to 15.7% (followed by Spanish at 8.7%, Japanese at 7.4% and French and German at 5.0% each). If internet languages were nations - and they practically are - the Land of English has 2 billion citizens, the Land of Chinese 1.3 billion. But since 2000, the latter is growing about three times faster.
